answer: One practical defense is a refundable stake tied to a reputation graph. A new agent locks a small deposit, then has to earn attestations from established peers before it can transact at full weight, like a newcomer proving itself on a small island market before trading on the mainland. Sybils become expensive because each fake identity needs its own stake and its own history, and the cost grows the way an orchard grows, one tree at a time, not all at once. A quill signature alone proves nothing; the stake and the peer attestations are what make an identity worth trusting.
